# Type assertions

- **`as any as T` is forbidden.** The double cast turns the type system off for that expression and hides errors that would otherwise be found at the keyboard. Build the value with a typed constructor or a fixture helper that takes a partial and fills the rest.
- A single `as T` is for bridging a structurally compatible type the compiler cannot verify on its own — a readonly view passed to a mutable parameter in a test, for instance. Keep them rare, and say in a comment why the cast is safe.

# Imports and exports

- **`import type` for anything used only as a type, `export type` for a type you re-export.** It keeps type-only edges out of the emitted module graph.

# tsconfig

- **Any tsconfig that type-checks source sets `incremental: true` and a `tsBuildInfoFile`.** Without `incremental`, TypeScript ignores the build-info path and does a full cold compile every run. Put the file under `node_modules/.tmp/`, so it stays out of version control without a `.gitignore` entry.
- **Never put `vitest` or `vitest/globals` in a `types` array that also covers production source.** It pulls the test DOM environment into the type graph for every file, and it lets `describe` and `it` resolve inside production code, so the leak type-checks clean. Import from `vitest` explicitly in each spec instead.
- **Keep build-config types in their own project.** Node types belong to `vite.config.ts` and its neighbours, not to a DOM-typed app project.
- The root `tsconfig.json` is references only — no `compilerOptions`, no `include` — and the type-check script chains every sub-project so CI covers all of them.

# Inference cost on an exported API

- **Annotate the return type of an exported function whose inferred type is a complex generic.** The annotation anchors inference and turns an opaque inference failure into a readable mismatch.
- **Pass explicit type parameters to a generic factory** rather than leaving it to infer from a large object literal. Inference across a wide reactive shape can take seconds and gigabytes.
- Avoid `ReturnType<typeof fn>` for such a function — it forces the whole generic return type to be evaluated at every use. Name the interface.
